title: Accurate measurements, the right ease, and a safe workspace

say: Accurate measurements, the right ease, and a safe workspace.
This is the video for Module 1 of Advanced Tailoring and Pattern Making.
Many of us learned to cut straight on the fabric with chalk. It works, but every garment starts from zero, and one cutting mistake ruins expensive fabric.

panel.heading: Cutting on fabric, or a paper block?
left: Hard to repeat or to teach
right: New styles start from a tested shape

say: A block is a plain, close-fitting shape on paper, with no style lines and no seam allowance. Once it fits, every new style starts from a tested shape.
For example, Bisi in Ibadan worked out that a block for her regular client Funmi pays for itself in the first year, and saves about 7.5 hours a year after that.

say: A 2 cm error at the bust gives a dress too tight to zip. First, check your tape against a metal ruler. 30 cm on the tape must be exactly 30 cm.

panel.heading: Fix three habits, gain accuracy
items: Check your tape against a metal ruler
Thin top, and the bra she will wear
Tie a tape at the natural waist
Tape snug and level, never tight

say: Measure over a thin top and the bra she will wear, because a padded bra changes the bust by several centimetres.

panel.heading: Fix three habits, gain accuracy
items: Check your tape against a metal ruler

Tape snug and level, never tight

say: Tie a narrow tape around her natural waist, the narrowest part, where the body bends sideways. Every length is taken to this line.

say: Keep the tape flat and level all the way round the back, with room to slide one finger under it. Do not add ease while measuring.

say: A 6 cm error would have made the bodice ride up. Two quick cross-checks saved a refitting. Date every card, and re-measure regular clients at least once a year.

panel.rule: Measure twice. A gap of more than 1 cm: measure again.

say: A pattern drafted exactly to the body is skin tight. The extra room you add on purpose is called ease. Wearing ease is the minimum room needed to move comfortably.

panel.heading: Room to breathe, sit and move
items: Wearing ease: room to move, built into the block
Design ease: extra room for style
Bust about 5 to 8 cm, waist about 2 to 4 cm
Hip about 4 to 6 cm, so she can sit

say: Design ease is extra room for style, plenty in a boubou, almost none in a mermaid gown.

say: For a fitted woven block, common starting points are about 5 to 8 cm at the bust, and about 2 to 4 cm at the waist.

panel.heading: Room to breathe, sit and move

Hip about 4 to 6 cm, so she can sit

say: And about 4 to 6 cm at the hip, or she cannot sit down. These are starting points, not laws. You confirm ease in the toile.

say: Most blocks are drafted as a quarter of the body, so you divide by four. For example, Ada drafts a fitted dress for a client with a 96 cm bust, and wants 6 cm of ease.

panel.heading: Ada turns body into pattern width
items: Body quarter: 96 / 4 = 24 cm
Ease per quarter: 6 / 4 = 1.5 cm
Block quarter: 24 + 1.5 = 25.5 cm
Check: 25.5 x 4 = 102 cm
Add 1.5 cm seam allowance at the side

say: Keep shears closed and pointing down when you carry them, and store rotary cutters with the guard on. Never hold pins in your mouth. They can be swallowed or inhaled.

panel.heading: Safe with blades, pins and power

cards.d: Carry shears closed, pointing down. Guard rotary blades. Never hold pins in your mouth.
Switch off before threading. Stand the iron on its heel; unplug when you leave.
Do not overload one extension socket. Use a stabiliser if power fluctuates.

say: Switch off the sewing machine before threading it or changing the needle. Stand the hot iron on its heel, unplug it when you leave the table, and keep the cord out of walkways.

say: Do not overload one extension socket with an iron and several machines. Keep a first aid box with plasters and burn gel.

say: To remember. Blocks are plain shapes. Measure snug, level and twice. Add ease on the pattern, divided by four. And measurements are private, so never post a client's card in a WhatsApp group without her permission.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A block has no seam allowance or style lines
Measure snug and level, over thin clothing
Measure twice; cross-check front and back
Divide total ease by four for a quarter block
Respect privacy: never share a client's card
